Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. content.text:
`include/hybrid` 是 QEMU plugin、vsim、driver 三方共用的 ABI 合約。對「build verilator」來說，需要的是其中一部分:

| Header | vsim binary (`src/`) | vsim unit tests | 誰還在用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_abi.h` | ✅ | ✅ | plugin, driver |
| `state_abi_check.h` | ✅ (被 `state_abi.h` 在 L117 include) | ✅ | plugin |
| `insn_match.h` | ✅ (`csr_trigger.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`) | ✅ | plugin |
| `handoff_site.h` | ❌ | ✅ (只有 test) | plugin |
| `v_drain_policy.h` | ❌ | ✅ (只有 test) | plugin |
| `reg_names.h` | ❌ | ❌ | **只有** plugin |

- 只 build **vsim 執行檔** → 3 個: `state_abi.h` + `state_abi_check.h` + `insn_match.h`
- 連 **unit tests** 一起 build → 再加 `handoff_site.h`、`v_drain_policy.h`，共 5 個
- `reg_names.h` verilator 完全不用 (只有 QEMU plugin 用)

---

## 關於「移出 verilator」

先講現況: `verilator/` **已經是 submodule** 了 (`.gitmodules` → `hybrid_vsim`)。真正的問題是它的 build 反向往上抓 parent 的 header:

```
verilator/CMakeLists.txt:455
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../include"   <- 伸手進 andesim 的 include/hybrid
```

2	// predicate runs in two places: the QEMU TCG plugin (C) and the vsim PC

6	// result, so it is an architectural NOP on every conforming core. Marker

9	// CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores and the exit marker enabled ILM at

/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
 *
 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
 * silently omits the V block when:
 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
 *
 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
 *
 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
 */
#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"  /* HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: the L11 ceiling */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
} HybridVDrainPolicy;

/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
 *
 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
 */
static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
{
    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (no V)
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=1            -> ABORT  (partial advertisement)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (nothing to drain)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb=0   -> SKIP   (V disabled at runtime)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb>MAX -> ABORT  (L11: wire format
     *                                            cannot hold this VLEN; never
     *                                            truncate silently)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, otherwise -> OK
     */
    if (!has_vlenb && has_other_v) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    if (!has_other_v)              return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value == 0)          return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value > HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK;
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif  /* HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H */

# andes-hybrid-abi

The shared wire-format contract for the Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator. These
headers define the bytes exchanged across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. They are
consumed by three independent components, so they live in their own repo and
are pinned as a submodule by each consumer (one source of truth, no drift):

| Consumer | Repo | Mounts this as |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `andesim` (QEMU TCG plugin + C++ driver) | top repo | `include/` |
| `hybrid_vsim` (vsim / SystemC + Verilator) | submodule | `external/hybrid-abi/` |

Both mount points put this repo's root on the include path, so every consumer
includes the same way:

```c
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
```

## Layout

```
hybrid/
  state_abi.h        struct hybrid_state_v1 -- the wire format
  state_abi_check.h  compile-time offset/size lock (static_assert)
  insn_match.h       handoff marker HINT recogniser
  handoff_site.h     translate-time trigger capture + post-trigger PC
  v_drain_policy.h   pure V-state drain gate decision
  reg_names.h        GDB register-name tables (gdbstub wire contract)
tests/
  abi_compile_check.{c,cpp}  include every header from C and C++
  check.sh                   compile both as C11 + C++20
```

## Contract rules

- Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host). Not
  endian-portable.
- Never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add fields by consuming
  bytes from `reserved`, or bump to v2. `state_abi_check.h` locks every offset;
  a layout change must update it in lock-step and bump `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`.
- Both C and C++ must keep compiling these headers.

## Test

```sh
tests/check.sh        # host gcc/g++, zero external deps
```

A pass means the headers are self-contained from the repo root and the
`hybrid_state_v1` layout matches the locked offsets.

## History

Started fresh at the submodule split; the pre-split history of these headers
lives in the `andesim` repo under `include/hybrid/`.

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
